How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment
for agenda items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per
person (six minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time
limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note
that interactions between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings
are subject to the City’s Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

MINUTES OF APRIL 7, 2026
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:30 P.M. on Tuesday, April 7, 2026, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  John Wu, Vice Mayor Eric Chan, and Mayor Denise
  Menchaca.
  Council Members Absent:  Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, Finance Director William
  Kaholokula, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Community
  Development Director David Sanchez, Public Works
  Director Michael Sledd, Fire Division Chief Newton Ong,
  and Assistant City Clerk Adam Yang .

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Assistant City Clerk Yang provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. POLICE DEPARTMENT PROMOTIONAL RECOGNITION

I  Police Chief Elizalde made the presentation recognizing the promotions of
  Lieutenant Tim Logan, Sergeant Gilbert Magana, and Sergeant Mike Messropian.

  B. AUTISM AWARENESS AND ACCEPTANCE MONTH

  Crime Prevention Officer Stacy Guitierrez and Officer Esther Tse presented the San
  Gabriel Police Department's Silent Day Out event, and Mayor Menchaca presented
  the proclamation to Sergeant Gilbert Magana, Crime Prevention Officer Stacy
  Guitierrez and Officer Esther Tse.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 3  April 7, 2026
   3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  A written comment was received from Dystanie Flores of the California Department of
  Insurance soliciting Council support of proposed Wildfire Recovery legislation: AB
  1795, SB 876, and AB 1680.

  Douglas Fraser commented on a claim he filed with the City over a parking citation.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

I  A motion was made by Council Member Wu, seconded by Vice Mayor Chan, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4D as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 3-0-0-2 as follows:

  AYES:  WU,CHAN,MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  DING, HERRERA AVILA

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of March
  17, 2026.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved March 6, 12, and 19, 2026, Material Demands for the

I  payment of City expenditures.
  C. THEATER RENTAL FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY ASIAN AMERICAN ADVOCACY
  ALLIANCE FOR THANKS USA EVENT

  The City Council granted a partial waiver of the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse
  rental fee in the amount of $4,200 for the May 9, 2026 performance and one day
  of rehearsal for the Asian American Advocacy Alliance's upcoming Thanks USA
  event.

  D. THEATER RENTAL  FEE WAIVER REQUEST  BY ASIAN  ARTS TALENTS
  FOUNDATION

  The City Counci l granted a partial waiver of the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse
  rental fee in the amount of $6,070 for the Asian Arts Talents Foundation's June 27
  community performance.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

I  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS - None.

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto reported that the Smith Park pool heater is being
  manufactured and installation will take place as soon as possible, and announced that
  the Farmer's Market will begin on April 11, 2026, but due to rain, the grand opening
  festivities are rescheduled to April 18, 2026.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 3  April 7, 2026
   9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Chan reported on his attendance at San Gabriel's Lunar Lantern Festival, a
  San Gabriel County Water District board meeting, San Gabriel's State of the City
  address, a multi-Chamber networking event, grand opening/ribbon-cutting for the
  Athen Services Materials Recovery Facility, annual Sierra Madre Wistaria Festival, and
  the Kiwanis Egg'straordinary Pancake Breakfast and Egg Hunt.

  Council Member Wu reported on his attendance at the North America Enshrinement

I  Ceremony of the sacred relics of Fo Guang Sha n's founding master, Venerable Master
  Hsing Yunat at Hsi Lai Temple, San Gabriel's Lunar Lantern Festival, and the
  Outstanding Youth Awards Ceremony hosted by the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent
  Association.

  Mayor Menchaca thanked everyone who participated in the State of the City event;
  commented on the Athens Services new facility, apt Kiwanis Egg'straordinary Pancake
  Breakfast and Egg Hunt, and San Gabriel Lunar Lantern Festival; encouraged the
  community to participate in the online Community Budget Priority Survey; and
  reported on a visit to new San Gabriel business Grapevine Central Wine Shop.

  She announced that the application period is open for City commissions until April
  10, 2026; commented on the new Farmer's Market; announced a San Gabriel Valley
  Symphony free concert on April 16, 2026; and reported that she was presented the
  Outstanding Female Role Model award by the Chinese Women's Business Association
  of California and that Assemblymember Mike Fong and community leader Florence
  Lin also received awards.

  In closing, she announced upcoming events for Memorial Day will include the annual

I  Memorial Day weekend ceremony; a free concert by the United State Air Force Band
  on May 18, 2026, at the Mission Playhouse which will also celebrate the 250th
  anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence; and the Field of Heroes
  at Plaza Park in conjunction with the San Gabriel Veterans' Memorial Coalition.

  10. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:17 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

  JULI
